newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-FAUMUINA WINS NEW ZEALAND'S FIRST WORLD GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FAUMUINA WINS NEW ZEALAND'S FIRST WORLD GOLD.

text.p: Beatrice Faumuina won New Zealand's first gold medal in the 14-year history of the world championships when she won the women's discus final on Thursday.

The 22-year-old of Samoan descent, who came into the competition as favourite after throwing a season's best of 88.52 metres at Oslo a month ago, fouled her first two throws and would have been eliminated if her third throw was illegal or too short.
But she survived the pressure to unleash her winning delivery of 66.82 metres in the third round.
That was good enough not only to win New Zealand's first world championship title, but also their first ever world medal.
Defending champion Ellina Zvereva of Belarus, who led the competition after two rounds with a heave of 65.90 metres, could not improve on that and had to settle for the silver.
Natalya Sadova of Russia, the Olympic silver medallist, took the bronze with a throw of 65.14 metres.

"I was looking forward to doing well here after failing to qualify for the Olympics last year, but I didn't think I could win gold," said Faumuina. "Of course I am absolutely delighted -- especially after last year's disappointment."
